Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. _Reviewed September 9, 2026, 10:55 PM ET / September 10, 2026, 02:55 UTC (Revision 3)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch adds guarded update admission, package rollback coordination, native service ownership checks, SQLite writer exclusion, and suppression of unrequested restart notices. > [!WARNING] > **SQLite table change** > > This PR modifies persisted SQLite tables in `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-storage.ts`. Prefer a design that avoids changing persisted SQLite tables. If the change is necessary, verify migration and upgrade compatibility against an existing database before merge. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 9 items remain** Keep open: this owner-assigned PR contains distinct recovery work, but executor authority does not reach the actual rollback mutations. The latest notice correction addresses the reported preservation failure at its producer; installed acceptance remains pending. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `ceb0674ac4d1701a2687119893313cf8b88c67b0` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Useful integration and focused controls remain limited by a concrete mutation-fencing gap and outstanding installed acceptance. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the executor and rollback owners need final-effect evidence for allowed execution, an unrelated executor, and original-helper loss during awaited package/service work. Current controls use a synthetic file effect or mocked package swap; the supplied installed result does not cover those refusals. The MEMBER exemption from unrelated contributor proof remains intact. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Needs proof | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: Authority-chain proof required: the executor and rollback owners need final-effect evidence for allowed execution, an unrelated executor, and original-helper loss during awaited package/service work. Current controls use a synthetic file effect or mocked package swap; the supplied installed result does not cover those refusals. The MEMBER exemption from unrelated contributor proof remains intact. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

## Accepted lossless capture contract, 2026-09-10

The maintainer approved the separate first-slice lossless database/config capture policy after explicit discussion of credentials, deleted/expired/free-page data outliving live retention, and continuing disk cost. This acceptance is additional to #143752's package-only design and does not add capture to that issue or transfer Vincent's implementation ownership.

The accepted component is lossless capture and verified reopening of required OpenClaw database/config resources, using the existing inventory, raw SQLite snapshot and writer-ownership code. It is not a whole-computer snapshot or delivered migration-crossing recovery.

- Private sibling `<stateDir>.update-captures/<captureId>/`; private ancestors/directories and owner-only files. One immutable manifest and numbered resources per artifact. No new mutable ledger or background service.
- Preserve exact config bytes and required raw database records/identities, including sensitive and deleted/free-page data. Ordinary backup sanitization remains unchanged.
- Exclude the exact managed capture root from ordinary backups and support exports before enabling capture, including selection through a containing or nested workspace. Explicit backup selection must not override that exclusion.
- Retain completed captures until explicit operator discard. No age/count pruning, automatic space-pressure retirement, or automatic adoption/deletion of crash-left artifacts. Crash leftovers are inspection-only. Only proven invocation-owned incomplete staging may be cleaned automatically.
- Check required/available capacity before capture and measure peak capture/staging cost. Capacity failure must preserve live data and earlier captures; retention has no invented size/time bound.
- Require complete known-owner resource/writer closure. Unknown writers/resources, conflicts, changed inventory or locators/content, lost authority and invalid publication refuse the whole capture. Preserve absence facts without bootstrapping stores. Copied leases or matching hashes are not authority, and finite proof is not universal writer safety.
- Reopen only after verifying the manifest and resource identities. This does not authorize replay into live state, overwriting newer data, whole-store restoration, or a rollback-success claim.

Process-scoped disposable snapshots remain the alternative when retained artifacts are not wanted. The component must reuse existing owners rather than the parked #137399/#137837 implementations. Separate capture/reopen and privacy exclusion from subsequent preparation/replay integration. Rollback of this feature must preserve existing artifacts for explicit inspection/discard, never delete them as part of uninstall or downgrade.

Validation requires focused capture/reopen/privacy/discard/refusal/healthy-path regressions, independent review, required checks, exact-head CI and applicable finite installed proof through the existing journey owner. Earlier source-bound synthetic results remain limited to their verified bytes/platforms; no full recovery or power-loss acceptance is implied.

The implementation PR will link this accepted decision. Package mutation files remain reserved to #143750 and the canonical package-only publisher remains separate under #143752.

Accepted lifecycle revision for the lossless capture follow-up: future automatic recovery sets are transaction-scoped, not an indefinite snapshot history. This supersedes that part of the earlier capture decision; the exact private managed root and mandatory backup/support exclusion are unchanged.

One unresolved set over the affected state blocks another. Capacity admission must include capture, package/recovery staging, possible growth and reserve before protected mutation. Insufficient capacity never authorizes deleting recovery or disabling protection. Unknown effects cannot justify skipping required databases; schema equality alone is insufficient.

Bulk recovery data becomes cleanup-eligible only after identity-bound runtime/data validation, readiness/stability, settled mutating children, no remaining recovery dependency and durable terminal success (or equivalent complete restoration proof). Persist that outcome before retirement. Interruption before it retains recovery; interruption during retirement resumes only identity-verified authorized cleanup. Corrupt/foreign records, locator changes or lost authority refuse. Age and disk pressure do not grant deletion authority.

Reuse existing lifecycle/retirement owners, not a new ledger/daemon/GC. Existing manual-retained captures, deliberate backups and historical evidence are not cleanup targets. Package-only repair remains package-only and cannot establish whole-update success. After verified cleanup, later rollback to the pre-update database state is no longer available.

The independent export-exclusion prerequisite does not create or clean captures. Production capture/terminal integration and its applicable installed proof remain separate work; this acceptance is not a claim they have shipped.

A merged follow-up, [#146865](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146865), improves the misleading inspection-unavailable diagnostic when the main process has stopped but observed tasks remain in the unit's cgroup. It reports the remaining task count and asks the owner to stop those children before retrying. The refusal remains unchanged: this does not alter safe package rollback or admission behavior. This is a diagnostic follow-up only; #140339 remains merged.
